- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment is negative but model ignores it).  
- Underestimate price peaks when sentiment is strongly negative (model fails to recognize downward momentum).  
- Overshoot after short-term spikes — model reacts too aggressively to recent highs.  
- Mean-reversion bias: model holds too much upward momentum even when sentiment shows cooling.  
- Lagged response to sentiment: model reacts to sentiment shifts 1–2 days too late.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative, reduce forecast slope — avoid upward drift.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model should not overreact — cap upward bias at 1–2% above recent mean.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid overfitting to recent 7–14 day trends — sentiment should override technical momentum.
